basis: Acute myeloid leukemia is a blood and marrow malignancy; GATA1 mutation does not establish additional organ involvement.
Platelet dysfunction and ocular/oculocutaneous albinism define these HPS types; pulmonary fibrosis is excluded and colitis is not established in >=30%.
Inherited complement deficiency; meningococcal infections are separate infectious episodes, not intrinsic neurologic damage.
Developmental disability and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; small extremities and delayed maturation do not establish locomotor damage.
Bardet-Biedl phenotype: retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and polydactyly; renal abnormalities in roughly half; common cognitive impairment omitted under the four-axis cap.
IRF9-associated immunodeficiency defines the disease; bronchiectasis and oral inflammation lack frequencies sufficient to establish common direct involvement.
Inherited lymphatic vascular malformation with impaired lymphatic drainage and lymphedema.
Peroxisomal fatty-acid disorder defined by cerebral demyelination; adrenal insufficiency is also very frequent. Visual and hearing impairment occur in <30%.
Carcinoma originates in the pharynx, explicitly assigned to the pulmonary axis.
Metabolic enzyme deficiency with defining liver disease and dental anomalies; hepatic failure and enamel defects occur in 80-99%.
Malignant hypertension causes arteriolar injury; advanced retinopathy is a classic diagnostic criterion, and renal injury occurs in roughly half or more.
Congenital humerus-radius fusion causes elbow immobility; ocular and CNS malformations occur in <30%.
Benign smooth-muscle tumor arising in the breast; breast has no axis and smooth muscle is not skeletal muscle.
Neurodegenerative parkinsonism with autonomic failure; bladder dysfunction, orthostasis and respiratory manifestations reflect neural dysfunction, without established direct organ injury.
Isolated spermatogenic failure causing azoospermia and infertility; reproductive dysfunction without established endocrine disease.
Congenital fusion of teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defined as childhood interstitial/emphysematous lung disease; additional FLNA-associated manifestations cannot be inferred from the gene alone.
Skin appendage and CNS defects define the syndrome; enamel abnormalities and microdontia occur in 80-99%; nonspecific immune annotation does not establish immunodeficiency.
Hypothalamic/neurodevelopmental and endocrine dysfunction define PWS; scoliosis in 150/180 and reduced muscle mass are common; strabismus occurs in 30-79%.
Sparse description supports a familial skeletal/muscle syndrome with dwarfism and painful spasms; endocrine deficiency or neurologic pathology is not established.
Psychiatric obsessive-compulsive disorder; no qualifying direct organ damage is established.
Airway ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis defines disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation in 2/2 supports otologic involvement; situs inversus does not imply cardiac damage.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 12/12.
Infantile epilepsy is a neurologic disorder despite typical remission; later movement disorders remain within the same axis.
Myoclonus, spastic paraparesis and cerebellar ataxia define a neurologic syndrome; motor manifestations do not establish primary muscle disease.
